records.trigger: ACC-001-explain-output: the acceptance claim of B-a745 is that an operator can run a read-only validation_plan command and see requestedTier, effectiveTier, a runtime-derived selected-of-total count, per-command inclusion reasons, unclassified inputs, glossed escalation reason codes, and finalAuthority: no.
records.observedFailure:
The acceptance-claim command does not exist. Running `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast --explain` on the story branch at baseline HEAD 3d86905687739cee312571b4bb504600debd0a59 prints:

  Unknown command: validation_plan
  Did you mean:
    proof-or-stop plan_skeleton
    proof-or-stop plan_set
    proof-or-stop plan_get
  Use proof-or-stop help to view all commands.

Nothing about the acceptance claim is satisfied: there is no tier vocabulary, no command identity, no pin resolution and no explain output. A SECOND, separable defect is visible in the same observation and is being recorded rather than fixed here: the CLI exits 0 on an unknown command, so a caller cannot detect this failure by exit code and must string-match stderr. That exit-code defect is out of scope for B-a745, whose planner is a new command rather than a change to the unknown-command path.
records.note: Recorded at the PLAN to DEV boundary, before any implementation commit, from a real observation rather than a predicted one. This is the story-level red state that the whole Story turns green. Per-item RED commits for CHK-001 through CHK-005 follow the same discipline inside DEV: each item's fixture is committed failing before its implementation, which CHK-006 verifies by asserting a failing-fixture commit precedes each implementation commit in git log. greenRelation is same_acceptance because the green command proves the very same acceptance target, not a regression guard for a different one.
